title: Story-beat ledger and style bible
description: The one cleanly unmet gap Phase 9.1 of road-to-frontend-fidelity-calibration verified: `grep -rilE 'beat ledger|story ledger|style bible' src/` returned zero paths on 2026-08-22. Hosted in `wireframe` because that skill already owns the low-fidelity artefact — a beat ledger IS a low-fidelity artefact, one axis further along than a static skeleton. No skill was created to hold a schema. Two halves in one file, deliberately: the ledger is what happens in order, the style bible is what it looks like throughout, and splitting them into two files would let a beat reference a style that no longer exists.

schema_version.description: Pinned. One-member `enum` rather than `const`: this repo's Draft-07 subset validator enforces `enum` and silently ignores `const`.

surface.description: The page or route the ledger describes.

style_bible.description: What holds STILL across every beat. A property that changes per beat belongs on the beat, not here — that split is the point of having a bible at all.

palette_ref.description: A token reference, never a literal. `brand-source-of-truth` governs: the consumer's registered tokens win over anything a bible proposes.

type_ref.description: Token reference for the type system, per `typography-system`.

motion_band.description: The motion band this surface sits in. `fe-design` § Motion is the timing source of truth; this names a band, it does not define one.

reduced_motion_presentation.description: What the surface presents INSTEAD of motion when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set. Required by convention on any bible whose beats carry `motion`: `animation: none` is a suppression, not a presentation. This field is the schema half of step 9.3.

art_direction_note.description: The brief-level direction a `design-director` read would judge against. Free text.

beats.description: Ordered. A scroll-driven surface is a sequence, and the order is the content.

id.description: Stable beat id. The scroll evidence artefact in `design-review/references/verification-automation.md` references these ids, which is what lets a review check a beat rather than a pixel row.

intent.description: What this beat is FOR, in one sentence. A beat with no intent is a section, and a wireframe does not need a ledger to list sections.

enters_at.description: Where the beat begins — a scroll fraction, a viewport-height multiple, or null when the ledger is authored before any layout exists. `null` is the honest value at wireframe stage and must stay allowed.

element_states.description: What is asserted to be true at this beat. The unit a review can check.

selector.description: A CSS selector, or a wireframe region name before markup exists.

state.description: The asserted state — `visible`, `pinned`, `faded`, `offscreen`, and so on. A vocabulary the reviewer and the ledger share, not a free-form description.

motion.description: The motion this beat uses, if any. A beat carrying this obliges `style_bible.reduced_motion_presentation` to say what replaces it.

maturity.description: Which axis of `design-fidelity` § Two axes this beat sits on. A `wireframe` beat carries a STRUCTURE mandate: its greys and its exact offsets are non-decisions and must not be reproduced 1:1. Present so a ledger cannot be handed over as a pixel spec by omission.
